reasons: Status is correctly classified as a deviation: p0149 is a blanket, one-sided bar on Licensee assignment with no affiliate/M&A carve-out, and Article XX(a) automatically terminates our license and rights on our own Change of Control absent Licensor consent (with consent deemed reasonably withheld whenever Licensor merely believes its interests are affected) — squarely at the playbook walk-away line.

Redline reaches the preferred position: (i) assignment to an Affiliate or M&A successor without consent, (ii) reasonableness standard for other Licensee assignments, (iii) Licensor assignment subject to our consent and never to a competitor, and (iv) removal of the Change-of-Control termination/consent/re-pricing right while preserving the 'CHANGE OF CONTROL' defined-term lead-in in p0134 so downstream cross-references survive.

Failed minimal-edit ratios on both paragraphs are acceptable here: the playbook requires replacing a prohibition with a carve-out and neutralizing an automatic CoC termination trigger, which cannot be achieved by small in-line insertions.
Comment is accurate, concise, correctly prefixed, first-person plural, explains the change, cites the playbook line, and offers the mutual-notice fallback.

Minor point to watch (not disqualifying): the rewrite of p0149 drops the original restriction on sublicensing/transfer of license rights, which is broader than the assignment issue and may draw counterparty pushback; consider retaining a sublicense consent requirement to keep the edit tightly scoped.
